(1) a simple model of constant-density, weakly ionized disc reflection fits the data as well as the more complex ionized disc models, and (2) the ionized disc models do not predict the strength of the soft O Kα line that has been claimed by the XMM-Grating Team.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reflection models are not yet fully developed and that the data are still insufficient to discriminate between different models.
the data are consistent with a weakly ionized disc model, but the ionized disc models cannot be ruled out.
the ionized disc reflection models are consistent with the data, but that a simpler model of reflection and a single line is equally consistent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data can be fitted by both the ionized disc and the weakly ionized disc models, and that both models have difficulties.
the ionized disc reflection model can fit the ASCA data of MCG-6-30-14.
the reflection spectrum of MCG-6-30-16 is consistent with a weakly ionized disc with a low iron abundance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Fe Kα line profile in MCG–6–30–15 is not as complex as has been previously thought.
the reflection spectra of AGN are complex and that it is not possible to model them with a single component, whether that component be ionized or neutral.

a simple model of reflection from an optically thick, neutral, constant-density disc with solar abundance is able to fit the hard X-ray data, and that this model should be considered when interpreting the X-ray spectrum of this source.
